author: kirubaharan181
description: Defines system boundaries, interfaces and trade-offs. Use when designing or reviewing architecture. Do NOT use for feature coding or release.
purpose: Produces reviewable architecture: boundaries, interfaces, data, security and cloud design, with the trade-offs and decisions recorded. It owns stages 23-34: solution, system, application, database, API, cloud, security, data and integration architecture, technology selection, documentation and architecture review.
when_to_use: A new system or major change needs structure, interfaces and quality targets designed.
A technology or integration choice needs evidence and a decision record.
An implemented system must be checked against its intended architecture.
when_not_to_use: Writing or changing feature code: use software-implementation.
Running threat tests or scans: use application-security.
prerequisites: Validated requirements with quality targets, or a stated list of assumptions.
Description of the current landscape and constraints.
Access to existing architecture records, if any.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: decision records with options and consequences
interface contracts and data ownership map

decision_rules.action: Ask for it or record an assumption; do not design against a word.
Choose the one that is cheaper to reverse and record the reopen condition.
Require a recovery objective that justifies it.

decision_rules.situation: Implemented system diverges from the design
decision_rules.action: Classify as accepted evolution, defect or risk, each with an owner.

quality_gates: Each quality target maps to a design element
Each significant decision has a record with rejected options
Interfaces have owners and versioned contracts
Review was by someone who did not design it

examples.title: Choose between two message brokers
examples.request: Pick a broker for order events.
examples.context: Peak 2,000 events per second, ordering per customer required, team knows neither.
examples.behavior: Write criteria and weights first, run a short proof of concept on ordering at peak, score both with evidence, and record the decision.
examples.output: ADR naming the chosen broker, rejected option, test evidence and the condition for reopening.
examples.acceptance: Criteria dated before scoring; proof of concept result attached.

examples.title: Review implemented architecture
examples.request: Check the billing service against the approved design.
examples.context: Approved design says only the orders service reads the orders database.
examples.behavior: Compare the import and data-access graph with the rules, list divergences and classify each.
examples.output: Conformance report with one risk finding: reporting module reads the orders database directly.
examples.acceptance: Each divergence has a class, owner and date.

limitations: Cannot measure real performance without test data or a proof of concept.
Does not approve its own designs: an independent reviewer and the architecture board do.
Cost estimates depend on provider prices that change.

troubleshooting.cause: Latency and cost targets cannot both be met
troubleshooting.resolution: Show the trade-off and ask the sponsor to choose.
Inspect code and deployment definitions, record findings as assumptions.
Add the condition to the decision record.

handoffs.artifact: decision records, interface contracts and dependency rules
architecture and data flows for threat modeling
